name: Dify
summary: Source-available platform for LLM apps and agent workflows: visual builder, RAG pipelines, model-agnostic. The Community Edition is free of a software fee to self-host, but you own the servers, updates and reliability.
best_for: technical teams that want to build and ship LLM apps and agents on a source-available platform they can self-host and control
skip_if: you want a no-maintenance, non-technical builder: a fully managed no-code AI tool saves you the infra and upkeep
honest_knock: 'Free' self-hosting isn't free: you own the servers, updates and reliability, and model usage bills separately once the included message credits run out. Dify Cloud takes that infrastructure work off your hands, but every cloud plan is a single workspace, and multiple workspaces, SSO and a commercial licence sit in quote-only Enterprise. It's powerful, but self-hosting it well needs technical comfort.

pricing.notes: Source-available and free of a software fee to self-host — the Community Edition ships under the Dify Open Source License, a modified Apache 2.0 with additional conditions — while the managed Dify Cloud adds a free Sandbox, Professional at $59/mo ($590/yr) and Team at $159/mo ($1,590/yr), each priced per workspace (re-verified 2026-10-09 against dify.ai/pricing.md; the advertised ~17% annual saving checks out: $590 against $708 and $1,590 against $1,908 at the monthly rate). Self-hosting still costs you infrastructure, model usage and any commercial licence those terms require. Cloud plans include message credits for supported model providers; once those run out you connect your own provider API key and pay that provider directly.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested Dify Cloud on the Sandbox plan: one chatbot built from a sample template and tried once in the preview. No own API key was used and nothing was published. The template Chatflow: AI Chatbot, which needed the model gpt-5.4-mini, was used through Create from this sample app. The editor opened with the nodes START, LLM and ANSWER and a visible system prompt, with the status Auto-Saved 17:50:49 and Unpublished. The preview question In two sentences: what should a small team check before buying an AI tool? was answered within about 8 seconds: whether the tool solves a real problem, ease of use, integrations, cost, privacy and support. No own API key was needed: the model ran on the credits included with Dify. Credits went from 200 to 195 after one answer, so 5 credits for that answer. From the home screen to a working chatbot took about 2 minutes. It needed no code and no server, but building it does require understanding the nodes (START, LLM, ANSWER) and the system prompt. Self hosting for technical teams was not tested, as no self hosted installation was made. The app stays unpublished in the Sandbox. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: One short answer used 5 credits of the 200 free credits, and building even a sample chatbot needs some understanding of nodes and the system prompt.

sessions.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 we tested Dify Cloud on the Sandbox plan: one chatbot built from a sample template and tried once in the preview. We used no API key of our own and published nothing. We did not test self-hosting, checkout, support or export.
findings: Sandbox is free and asked for no card. It starts with 200 message credits.
We created the sample app 'Chatflow: AI Chatbot' (model gpt-5.4-mini) from a template. The editor showed three nodes, START, LLM and ANSWER, and a visible system prompt.
The preview answered our question in about 8 seconds, on the credits Dify includes. One answer cost 5 credits (200 to 195). From the home screen to a working chatbot took about 2 minutes.
No code and no server were needed. Changing the bot does mean understanding the nodes and the system prompt.
Monthly prices we saw with the yearly toggle off: Professional $59 and Team $159 per workspace.
